prompt.brief: Design a real-time multimodal moderation platform that classifies text, images, and video across languages, applies policy decisions quickly, and routes uncertain or high-impact cases to human review.
successSignals: Keep submitted content and policy version authoritative while deriving model scores, decisions, reviewer queues, and appeals.
Use a fast rules-and-model cascade for text and images, with asynchronous frame sampling for video and language-specific thresholds.
Make decisions explainable enough for appeals, prevent model updates from changing historical evidence, and fail closed for severe risks.
Explain false positives, adversarial content, reviewer safety, privacy, regional policy, model rollout, and deletion.

functional: Submit content for pre- or post-publication checks, classify policy categories, quarantine risky content, and return a versioned decision.
Route low-confidence cases to reviewers, support appeals and overrides, and expose evidence, confidence, policy, and model versions.
Support language and region policies, user reports, deletion, audit export, reviewer permissions, and model evaluation feedback.
nonFunctional: Target p95 text moderation below 200 ms and make high-risk actions deterministic even when deeper video analysis is pending.
Process 100,000 pieces per second with modality and tenant queues that isolate viral content and large videos.
Make content submission, scoring, quarantine, review assignment, and decision publication idempotent.
Fall back to strict rules and quarantine for severe categories when model workers or feature services are unavailable.
scaleAssumptions: Moderate 100 million text items, 10 million images, and 1 million short videos per day across many languages.
Partition by tenant, content ID, modality, language, and policy region; isolate viral items and review queues.
Retain redacted content references, policy decisions, model versions, reviewer actions, appeals, and audit evidence.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Real-time multimodal moderation platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Real-time multimodal moderation platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Real-time multimodal moderation platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Real-time multimodal moderation platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Real-time multimodal moderation platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Real-time multimodal moderation platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Real-time multimodal moderation platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Real-time multimodal moderation platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Real-time multimodal moderation platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
